review_policy: reviewed means every capture cited for the operation replays against the node with no difference, or with differences that only the deliberate gaps the operation lists account for, and at least one is cited, for the cases those captures cover; it never means exhaustive equivalence. known_gap names a difference a replay observes, and the capture's replay lists it exactly. not_reviewed means the cited captures, if any, don't settle the operation, even if the node routes it.

timestamped-signatures-only.text: Every signed operation: upstream also accepts a request whose auth chain signs only its method and its path below /v1 (lowercased), whatever x-identity-timestamp or x-identity-metadata header the request carries or omits, valid until the delegated key expires. The node accepts only the timestamped payload over its own method and path, at most five minutes old and one minute ahead, and refuses such a request with upstream's 401 {ok:false, data:{message}, error:'Unauthenticated'}.

signature-window.text: Every signed operation: upstream accepts a timestamp up to 30 minutes old or ahead; the node accepts at most 60 seconds old and 60 seconds ahead, the window of every signed route on the node, and refuses the rest with the same 401.

unauthenticated-message.text: Every signed operation: when a signature does not verify, upstream's data.message is its verifier's own text, which includes the payload it expected and its local clock; the node's is a fixed text naming the failed check (Invalid auth chain, Invalid timestamp, Expired signature, Invalid signature). The status, error and envelope are upstream's, and no client reads data.message.

chain-copy-lag.text: Every operation that reads a collection's published or approved state, or a minted item's chain values (its URN, price, beneficiary, rarity, supply and content hash, read from the copy of the subgraph's items the shop's items mirror keeps): upstream asks the Polygon collections subgraph on each request; the node reads its copy of that subgraph, which the shop's collections mirror refreshes every three times MARKETPLACE_MIRROR_INTERVAL_SECS (15 minutes at the default 300). A collection deployed outside the node's own publication flow reads as unpublished, and an approval or a role change as not made, until the next pass, so a client that polls after a deployment (the old builder web retries its publish every 5 seconds) waits up to that bound plus the subgraph's lag. When the copy has no complete pass the node answers 503, and when its last pass, or the row or absence a decision reads, is more than 30 minutes old it answers 503 to every request that grants access or writes. A standard collection deployed outside the node's own publication flow within that window still reads as a draft, so its owner can save it: a save that changes its name or calldata gives the row another computed address, and the row no longer maps to the deployed contract. Upstream refuses such a save by asking the Polygon RPC whether the stored address holds a contract, and by the day-long lock the old builder sets right after its deployment.

owner-is-the-chain-creator.text: Every operation that decides by a standard collection's owner: once the node's copy of the Polygon collections subgraph holds the collection, its owner is the chain creator for every check; before, the stored eth_address. Upstream compares the stored eth_address in some checks and the chain creator in others until an owner sync rewrites the row, so between a creator transfer and that sync a client of upstream sees the previous creator keep, and the new creator lack, part of the owner's access; the node gives all of it to the chain creator at once.

managers-from-chain-only.text: Every operation that admits an on-chain manager or answers a collection's managers and minters: the node reads managers and minters only from its copy of the Polygon collections subgraph, so only a collection on chain has them, and a PUT /v1/collections/:id body never sets them. Upstream also stores the managers and minters such a body carries for a collection that is not on chain, answers them and admits those managers.

access-checks-never-write.text: DELETE /v1/items/:id, POST /v1/items/:id/files, POST /v1/items/:id/videos, POST /v1/collections/:id/lock, POST /v1/collections/:id/tos and DELETE /v1/collections/:id: the node's access check changes no row. Upstream's can set a collection's stored eth_address, and its items', to the chain creator when they differ, so a later read of those rows names the creator.

access-before-kind-conflict.text: PUT /v1/collections/:id on an existing collection: the node answers 401 Unauthorized to upsert collection before it compares the body's URN with the stored collection, so only a signer who may save the collection gets the 409s for converting it or changing its third party. Upstream answers those 409s first.

committee-cache.text: GET /v1/committee and every committee decision: the node reads the Polygon committee index (the Committee contracts' MemberSet logs) up to its published block afresh for each request, so a member added or removed counts once the index publishes the block that holds the change. Upstream reads the Polygon collections subgraph's accounts on every GET /v1/committee and keeps its own read an hour for decisions.

committee-unavailable.text: Every operation a committee member may perform: while the committee index is unpublished, published more than 30 minutes ago or unreadable, the node answers 503 to GET /v1/committee and to every decision only the committee could grant, and a committee member reads published content as any signer does. Upstream answers GET /v1/committee with an empty list and treats nobody as a member when its subgraph can't answer.

collection-list-bounds.text: GET /v1/collections, GET /v1/addresses and GET /v1/:address/collections: the node answers at most 1,000 rows (the committee's listing, the public search and the addresses) or 5,000 rows (an address's own listing) per response, with or without page and limit, and a page's limit above that is answered with the cap as its limit. It refuses with 400 a q longer than 256 characters, more than 5 tag values, a tag longer than 64 characters, a repeated page, limit, q, sort, type or is_published, a type other than standard or third_party, and a negative page or limit, and matches q literally, % and _ included. Upstream answers every matching row, reads % and _ in q as wildcards, and answers those inputs otherwise.

address-listing-transferred.text: GET /v1/:address/collections: a collection whose stored owner is the address but whose chain copy names another creator and neither the address as manager or minter is left out of the results, of total and of the status counts. Upstream leaves it out of the results only, after paging, so its total and counts include it, the page that held it answers one row fewer and each later page starts one row further on than the node's.

collection-save-input.text: PUT /v1/collections/:id: the node refuses with 400 Invalid request body a body key the schema doesn't name, a blank name, a urn that is not a whole collection URN, a string field over 256 characters, a managers or minters list over 1,000 entries and data over 1 MiB. Upstream drops keys its schema doesn't name, accepts those values.

initialize-data-creator.text: PUT /v1/collections/:id for a standard collection: the node computes the contract address only from data that is initialize calldata naming the signer as the collection's creator, and refuses other data with 409 Cannot upsert a collection without a valid data, after it has checked who may save the collection. Upstream computes the address from any data string.

invalid-body-detail.text: PUT /v1/collections/:id, PUT /v1/items/:idOrURN, POST /v1/collections/:id/tos and PATCH /v1/thirdParties/:id and POST /v1/collections/:id/validation-result with a body the schema refuses: each answers 400 {ok:false, data, error:'Invalid request body'}; PATCH and POST /v1/collections/:id/curation and PATCH /v1/items/:id/curation answer 400 {ok:false, data, error:'Invalid schema'}. Upstream's data lists its JSON schema validator's errors, the node's is {}.

admin-addresses-not-admitted.text: GET /v1/collections/:id, GET /v1/items/:id and GET /v1/collections/:id/items: upstream answers its ADMIN_ADDRESSES wallets the full body of a published collection and of an item, and every item of any collection; the node gives BUILDER_ADMIN_ADDRESSES no role on collection and item reads, and answers those wallets as any other signer: the public body, and 401 for a draft collection's items.

polygon-mainnet-collections.text: GET and PUT /v1/collections/:id and both listings: the node computes a standard collection's address with the Polygon mainnet collection factory and answers urn:decentraland:matic: collection URNs. Upstream deployed against a test network (CHAIN_NAME Sepolia) uses the Amoy factory and amoy URNs.

stored-name-trimmed.text: PUT /v1/collections/:id and PUT /v1/items/:idOrURN: the node stores and answers a collection's or an item's name trimmed of surrounding spaces; upstream stores it as sent and answers it so, also in a refusal's data.

query-never-overrides.text: GET /v1/:address/collections and GET and PUT /v1/collections/:id: the node takes the address and the id from the path, and a PUT's collection and data from its JSON body, whatever the query string carries; upstream reads an address, id, collection or data query parameter before the path or body. No client sends one: the old builder web, the marketplace and this repository's clients put only the listing filters in the query string.

item-upload-named-files.text: POST /v1/items/:id/files: the node reads each part's field name as the content hash of the part's bytes and stores the file only when the bytes hash to it and the item names that hash in its contents, and refuses any other part with 400 before it stores anything, as well as a part whose hash the item names only at video.mp4 (400 The video is uploaded through the videos route), which comes through POST /v1/items/:id/videos and its container check. Upstream stores every file under the hash it computes, whatever the field name, and ties no file to the item. The old builder web saves the item first and sends each file under the hash the item names.

item-upload-bounds.text: POST /v1/items/:id/files: the node takes at most 256 parts, empty ones included, and 20 MiB in all per upload, refusing more parts with 400 Too many files and more bytes, a file's or the whole request body's, with 413 The upload is too large, and reads no more of the body once a bound is passed; a body that hasn't arrived 5 minutes after the node began reading it answers 408 The upload timed out and frees its place. Before it reads the body it also refuses, with 429 and Retry-After at once, an upload while 16 are in flight, while the same wallet has four or while the same upload source (an IPv6 address widened to its /48) has eight. Upstream takes any number of files of up to AWS_MAX_FILE_SIZE each (26,214,400 bytes by default, 5,000,000 in its production settings) and answers a larger file with 500 File too large (multer's LIMIT_FILE_SIZE through its error handler, which carries no status); the node's gateway answers a body over 21 MiB on this path with 413, so the node's 413 is the status a client meets either way. The most files one item names in the reference data is 198.

item-list-bounds.text: GET /v1/collections/:id/items and GET /v1/:address/items: the node answers at most 20,000 items per response, with or without page and limit, a page's limit above that answered as 20,000, orders an address's items by creation then id, and refuses a negative page or limit and a collectionId that is neither a UUID nor null with 400; GET /v1/items, the committee's, answers what upstream answers (every item of every kind, with its chain state) bounded to the 1,000 oldest by creation then id, standard items first. Upstream answers up to 100,000 rows per response, every item on GET /v1/items, and an address's items in the database's order. github.com/decentraland/builder at 0ffcfbbb never calls GET /v1/items: its fetchItems takes an address (src/modules/item/actions.ts, src/lib/api/builder.ts), so the bound only reaches other committee tooling. The largest collection in the reference data holds 12,665 items and the largest owner 12,669; the old builder web asks for pages of 1 to 60. Each of those listings answers at most 64 MiB of item documents; past it 413 {ok:false, data:{maxBytes}, error:'The listing is too large, ask for it in pages'} before any item is read (the largest collection in the reference data holds 19.8 MB).

item-save-input.text: PUT /v1/items/:idOrURN: beyond builder-server's schema, the node refuses with 400 Invalid request body a contents value that is not a content hash, a contents key that is not a relative file path, more than 256 contents entries, mappings under a network the schema doesn't name or for a contract key that is not an address, more than 100 mapping entries or more than 10,000 token ids in them, an empty price or beneficiary, a name blank once trimmed, more than 1,000 tags or required permissions, a tag, required permission, file name or spring bone name longer than 1,000 characters, more than 10 representations, more than 256 files in a representation, more than 100 entries in a list of hidden or replaced categories or of body shapes, and more than 256 spring bone models or 1,000 bones in one; a body over 256 KiB answers 413 unread. Upstream stores them (mappings it can't name as an empty object) and takes bodies of up to 5 MB. The largest item document in the reference data is 27,136 bytes, with 117 tags of up to 208 characters and 98 files in a representation.

item-files-from-disk.text: GET and HEAD /v1/storage/contents/:hash: upstream answers every request with 301 to its bucket (<bucket>/contents/<hash>, a text/plain body naming the target, an immutable public Cache-Control). The node keeps item files on its own disk and answers a file it serves itself: 200, or 206 for a Range, with the file's bytes and its Content-Type read from the bytes, never from the upload (an attachment unless it is a media type, always nosniff and sandboxed), cached publicly for an unsigned request and private, no-store for a signed one. A client that follows the redirect receives the same bytes.

item-files-private-until-published.text: The node serves an unpublished item's file only to its readers. Each name in an item is attributed to the wallet whose save wrote it, and a name counts only while that wallet holds an upload record for the hash. An unsigned request gets a file only while a published item (a standard item once its collection is on chain, a third-party item once it has an item curation) names it in a name that counts; a signed request also gets a file its signer uploaded, or one that an item it owns, or a third-party item whose collection it manages, names in a name that counts. Any other request gets the 404 a hash with no file gets. Upstream redirects every request to its public bucket, so a client that loads a draft's file without a signature must sign that request.

item-files-absent.text: GET /v1/storage/contents/:hash of a hash the node holds no file for: upstream redirects it to its bucket like any other hash; the node answers 404 with the error envelope and Cache-Control: no-store.

item-files-exists-private.text: GET /v1/storage/contents/:hash/exists answers 200 {ok:true} only for a file the caller may read as GET /v1/storage/contents/:hash decides (deliberate gap item-files-private-until-published), and 404 {ok:true} for any other, a private file included. Upstream's probe answers 200 for any file its bucket holds.

rarities-read.text: GET /v1/rarities and GET /v1/rarities/:name: the node answers from one read of the Polygon collections subgraph's rarities and the rarities-with-oracle contract's price of each, kept one minute, and from no read of a name a request brings. When either source can't answer, or the subgraph lists no rarity, more than 100 or a malformed one, the node answers 503 {ok:false, data:{}, error:'The rarities are not available. Try again later.'} and asks again after 30 seconds. Upstream reads both on every request, answers an empty list when the subgraph fails and 404 'Could not fetch rarity from blockchain' when the oracle does.

item-contents-public-files-only.text: GET /v1/items/:collectionAddress/:itemId/contents: the node answers only a standard collection's item, and leaves out every entry whose file an unsigned GET /v1/storage/contents/:hash would answer 404 (a name whose writer holds no upload record for its hash, a hash the node withholds), and a smart wearable's video.mp4 when its kept video is such a file (a video another wallet wrote without holding the bytes). Upstream answers every entry of the item's row, and the kept video.

addresses-published-only.text: GET /v1/addresses: the node lists only published standard collections, so without is_published=true it leaves out every draft's precomputed contract address, and is_published=false lists nothing. Upstream also lists the drafts unless is_published=true is sent, and only the drafts with is_published=false.

lock-owner-only.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/lock signed by a wallet that may act on the collection but is not the owner of a standard collection (an on-chain manager, the provider manager of a third-party collection): upstream answers 200 with the date and stores no lock; the node answers 401 'Unauthorized user <signer> for collections <id>' and stores nothing. The old builder web locks only as the owner, right after it deploys.

publish-repeat-items-merged.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/publish of a standard collection whose items all hold their on-chain ids: upstream answers each item as its stored row, without the chain's values (is_published false, urn null, and its stored price, beneficiary, rarity, supply and content hash); the node answers the items merged with its chain copy, as on the call that assigned the ids. The old builder web reads only the items' on-chain ids from the answer.

owner-sync-stores-nothing.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/owner/sync: upstream writes the chain creator into the collection's and its items' stored eth_address when they differ; the node stores nothing, since it reads the owner from its chain copy on every request, and answers the same body. A later read of an item's stored eth_address shows the difference. The old builder web never calls the route.

third-party-claims.text: A provider the registry lists unapproved whose virtual third party lists other wallets: the node admits as its manager only a wallet both list, and refuses the others (401); upstream admits the virtual third party's managers alone until the registry approves the provider. The old builder web registers a provider from its virtual third party with the same managers, so both list them; a wallet that claimed an id before another wallet registered it on chain manages nothing of it on the node.

curation-invalid-id.text: GET, PATCH and POST /v1/collections/:id/curation, GET /v1/collections/:id/itemCurations and GET, PATCH and POST /v1/items/:id/curation with an id that is not a UUID: upstream hands it to its database, whose error answers 200 {ok:false, data:{}, error:<the database's message>}; the node answers 400 {ok:false, data:{id}, error:'Invalid uuid <id>'}, as its other routes do. No client sends one.

curation-input.text: PATCH /v1/collections/:id/curation and PATCH /v1/items/:id/curation: the node answers 400 to a body without curation (upstream 200 {ok:false, error:'Could not get curation from request'}) and 400 Invalid schema to an assignee on an item's curation (upstream fails in its database and answers 200 {ok:false}). The old builder web always sends curation, and never an item's assignee.

fixed-capture-clock.text: A curation row written twice during the capture run: upstream ran on the capture's fixed clock, so a row created and later updated in the run reads the same created_at and updated_at there; the node stamps each write with its own clock, as upstream does outside the capture, so updated_at is later. Two curation rows written in the run share one created_at there, so upstream's newest curation is ambiguous: after an appeal it read the earlier rejected row and accepted a second appeal, which the node refuses with 409 as upstream does on a real clock.

item-curation-reopened-by-the-committee.text: PATCH /v1/items/:id/curation with status pending on an item whose newest curation is approved or rejected, by a wallet off the committee: upstream sets that decision back to pending; the node answers 401 Only committee members can approve or reject a curation and writes nothing. The old builder web sends a pending PATCH only for an item whose newest curation is already pending, and asks again for a decided one with POST /v1/items/:id/curation.

curation-list-bounds.text: GET /v1/curations and GET /v1/collections/:id/itemCurations: the node answers at most 20,000 rows, above the committee's listing (3,502 collections) and the largest collection's item curations (12,665 items) in the reference data; upstream answers every row. GET /v1/collections/:id/itemCurations also refuses more than 20,000 itemIds with 400 and leaves out an itemIds value that is not a UUID, where upstream's database fails.

curation-notice-names.text: The curators' Slack notices name a person by a link labelled with the shortened address; upstream labels it with the profile name the catalyst holds for the address when it claimed one. A collection's name in a notice is cut to 300 characters.

curation-unknown-key.text: PATCH /v1/collections/:id/curation and PATCH /v1/items/:id/curation refuse a curation key the schema doesn't name with 400 Invalid schema, where upstream drops it and goes on; POST /v1/collections/:id/curation refuses a key other than assignee and note, and an assignee that is not a string, which upstream takes. The old builder web sends only status or assignee, and assignee or nothing.

forum-reply-mentions.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/curation/post: the node follows each @ with a zero-width space in the forum reply, so the text mentions no account or group. Upstream forwards the raw text unchanged. The old builder's assignment and unassignment notices contain no mention.

forum-reply-fields.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/curation/post: the node refuses unknown outer fields and unknown forumPost fields; raw and an ignored topic_id are accepted. At github.com/decentraland/builder-server 98897af, src/Curation/Curation.router.ts createCurationNewAssigneePost extracts only forumPost.raw and ignores other fields. The node test a_reply_is_refused_in_builder_servers_order_before_the_forum_is_asked covers outer and nested category fields, including mutation proofs of both parser rules. This difference is source-verified and node-tested, not recorded in an upstream capture.

cheque-salt-reused.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/publish of a third-party collection: a cheque whose salt its provider already used in a stored cheque is refused with 400 {ok:false, data:{id}, error:'An error occurred trying to publish: the cheque was already used'} and nothing is written; upstream stores the second cheque and submits the items, though the registry consumes a salt once. The node also stores each cheque lowercased with a 65-byte signature whose v is 27 or 28 (a 64-byte compact signature expanded), so approvalData answers that spelling.

third-party-publish-input.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/publish of a third-party collection: itemIds must be a list of at most 20,000 item ids, else 400 'Invalid request body', where upstream answers HTTP 200 {ok:false} with its database's error; the node refuses a high-s cheque signature and answers a cheque whose salt or signature doesn't read with 'Error: invalid salt' or 'Error: invalid signature' after upstream's message instead of its library's text; it refuses an item naming a file its name's writer never uploaded with 400 '<name>: upload missing content before publishing', and an item with no content hash with 409; and it never reads itemIds or the cheque from the query string. No legitimate client sends these.

third-party-registry-unavailable.text: GET /v1/collections/:id/approvalData: when the third-party registry can't be read, or its receipts answer is unreadable, the node answers 503; upstream answers HTTP 200 {ok:false} with the error.

third-party-publish-forum-after-commit.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/publish of a third-party collection: when the forum call after the submission fails or takes longer than 45 seconds, the node answers the committed publish as a success and logs the failure, and the next publish or POST /v1/collections/:id/post makes the topic; upstream answers HTTP 200 {ok:false} with the forum's error although the submission is stored.

catalyst-is-this-node.text: Item bodies and the third-party URN check read the node's own content as the catalyst: the active wearable or emote entity at the item's URN (a third-party item's own, matched exactly to the entity's metadata id; a minted item's on the chain copy, matched ignoring case), never an entity the node withholds. Such an item answers in_catalyst true; a third-party one is also approved and published with its entity's merkleProof.entityHash as catalyst_content_hash, and a minted one takes the entity's URN. When the node holds no entity at the URN, a body answers in_catalyst false and its node-recorded state, also while the node can't yet tell that no peer holds one; this is never answered with 503. A third-party save that claims a new URN refuses one the node holds with upstream's 409, and answers 503 'The catalyst's items are not available. Try again later.' and writes nothing while the node can tell neither way: it isn't its own content authority and its content sync hasn't proven, within 30 minutes of a pass's start, that it holds the peers' whole wearable and emote history. Upstream asks one configured catalyst over HTTP and treats its empty answer as unused.

item-curation-reopen-later-reads.text: After the provider's manager asked, as capture 428 does, to set an item's decided curation back to pending, which the node refuses (item-curation-reopened-by-the-committee), a later read of that item or of an item of its collection answers the mapping flag of the curation the node kept, where upstream answers that of the curation it reopened.

validator-pull.text: A standard collection's first publication, unapproved on chain, and a creator's changes submission on a published standard collection request its automated review. Upstream publishes the validation manifest to its events topic in the background, after answering. The node records a validation request (its item ids) in the transaction that publishes or submits, and the wearable validator pulls it: POST /v1/validator/claims answers the oldest claimable request's manifest, built from the items as saved when claimed, with a claimId and a 30-minute lease; POST /v1/validator/claims/:validationId/lease extends the lease, up to two hours after the claim; the result names its claimId. The replay claims every request the node recorded and compares the manifest with the one upstream queued.

validator-claim-id.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/validation-result: the node's body also carries the claimId of the claim the result answers, which upstream's schema refuses. A body without it answers 400 {ok:false, data:{}, error:'Invalid request body'} before its collection is compared with the path's. A result whose claim is not its request's current one (another claim, a lapsed or superseded lease, a settled request) or that names no request answers 204 and settles nothing.

validator-signature-binds-route.text: The validator's calls: upstream's x-wearable-validator-signature is the HMAC-SHA256 of `timestamp.rawBody`; the node's is of `timestamp.METHOD.path.rawBody` over the path the validator requested, the timestamp is Unix milliseconds in digits within five minutes either way, and a signature the node has seen within its window is refused, each with upstream's 401 {ok:false, data:{}, error:'Unauthorized'}. The replay signs each capture with the node's scheme and the capture's defect.

validator-switch.text: Upstream requests automated reviews while its builder-auto-curation flag is on and its events topic is configured, and answers the validator's callback whatever the flag. The node records requests, and its validator routes answer, only while WEARABLE_VALIDATOR_CALLBACK_SECRET is set and the builder flags document, with this node's overrides, has builder-auto-curation on; otherwise those routes refuse as an unsigned call.

validator-write-gate.text: With CREATE_WRITES_ENABLED off the validator's claim, lease and result answer 503 as every write does, and the job that settles requests does nothing; a refused result leaves its lease to lapse, and the request is claimed again once writes are on.

validation-request-bounds.text: Upstream sends a request each time and refuses a manifest over 50 items or 240 KiB with a curators' notice naming both. The node keeps at most one open request per collection (a newer one supersedes it), records at most five per collection a UTC day, and records none over 50 items, telling the curators 'it is too large for the automated review (N items)'. A request is abandoned after its third lapsed lease and expires when unsettled for seven days, each with the curators' notice that the collection needs a review without it; settled requests are deleted after thirty days.

validator-call-bounds.text: The validator's three routes take at most 60 calls a minute per source address that names a single client (none behind a gateway HTTP_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS doesn't list) (429 {ok:false, data:{}, error:'Too many requests, try again in a minute'}), a claim or lease body of at most 4 KiB and a result body of at most 5 MiB (413). A result's request must belong to the path's collection and name every item the result names (400), its validationId and each itemId must be a UUID in its canonical text, and nothing of it is stored but its outcome.

item-video-named-part.text: POST /v1/items/:id/videos: the node takes one file part, under the field video.mp4, and stores it only when its bytes hash to the hash the item names at video.mp4, which it checks again in the transaction that stores it; it refuses any other form with 400 before it stores anything: another field name, a part that isn't a file, a second part, no part, or bytes the item doesn't name. Upstream stores every file part under the hash it computes, whatever the field name, and ties no file to the item. The /create dApp saves the item first and sends its video as video.mp4.

item-video-container.text: POST /v1/items/:id/videos: the node walks the video's top-level MP4 boxes as they arrive and refuses with 400 The video is not an MP4 file, storing nothing, a file that doesn't begin with an ftyp box, has no moov box, or whose boxes don't end where the file does. Upstream stores any bytes under the content type the client sends; the node serves a stored file under the type its bytes show. Both publications take a file named video.mp4 as uploaded only when the videos route stored it, and an approval pins only such a video as a smart wearable's.

item-video-bounds.text: POST /v1/items/:id/videos: the node takes a video of up to 250,000,000 bytes, upstream's AWS_MAX_VIDEO_SIZE default, and refuses a larger one with 413 The video is too large and data.maxBytes, reading no more of the body; upstream answers 500 File too large. Before it reads the body the node also refuses an item that names no video (400), and with 429 and Retry-After an upload while its 32 places (BUILDER_VIDEO_UPLOADS_MAX, 1 to 256) are held, while the same wallet has one in flight or the same upload source (an IPv6 address widened to its /48) two, and while the wallet has spent its 4 hours or the source its 12 hours of upload time of the day (each upload charged the time it took once its body arrived or it ended); while reading it refuses part headers and framing over 64 KiB with 400, and answers 408 The upload timed out when the body hasn't arrived 20 minutes after the node began reading it or no byte came for 30 seconds. A declared Content-Length past the route's body (251,048,576 bytes) is refused at once with that 413, before the upload takes a place. While every place is held, a new upload takes the place of the upload whose wallet or upload source spent the longest on finished uploads today, if longer than the newcomer's; an upload whose wallet and source finished none today keeps its place until it ends. The upload that gives way ends with 408 The upload gave its place to another while the node was busy and Retry-After 30. Upstream bounds none of these. review-flow-switch.text: The review routes and the review flow's effects: upstream's flow is on while its builder-auto-curation and builder-auto-curation-review-flow flags are truthy and its events topic is configured. The node's is on only while WEARABLE_VALIDATOR_CALLBACK_SECRET is set and the builder flags document, with this node's overrides, holds both flags as the boolean true; off, the four review routes answer 404 Not found after the signature and change nothing, and a verdict only settles its request.

review-timeline-unreadable-as-absent.text: GET /v1/collections/:id/events: a signer who holds no role on the collection and is not on the committee gets the 404 an absent collection gets (Couldn't find ... on collections, with the id and table name); upstream answers such a signer 401 Unauthorized for an existing collection, which tells it the collection exists.

review-text-bounds.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/comments and .../curation/appeal: a collection takes at most 200 comments and 5 appeals in a UTC day and a wallet writes at most 200 comments and 20 appeals in a UTC day across collections (an appeal recorded by a changes submission counts too); beyond, 429 {ok:false, data:{id, retryAt}} with the next UTC day. Upstream bounds only the rate per wallet.

review-access-before-body.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/comments: the node decides who may comment before it reads the body, so a signer without a role and outside the committee gets 401 for any body; upstream checks the body's schema first and answers such a signer 400 for an invalid body.

review-running-is-an-open-request.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/validations and a creator's changes submission with the review flow on: an automated review runs while the collection has an open validation request (claimed or not) that no curator decision followed, and a retryable error from the validator keeps it open for the validator's next claim. A creator's request while it runs answers 409; at 5 requests of the collection in the UTC day it answers 429 with retryAt, counting every request. Upstream counts a run as running from its start event until its verdict within 7 days, frees a retryable error for the creator's retry, and counts the day's starts since the newest curator decision, sweep re-sends left out. GET /v1/collections with the review flow on lists such a collection, its newest curation pending, as auto_reviewing and not as pending, to_review or under_review.

review-timeline-from-requests.text: The review timeline with the flow on: the node records a start when it records a validation request and never a sweep re-send or a publish_failed error (the validator pulls its work; a lapsed claim is claimed again); a request abandoned after three lapsed claims or expired after 7 days records review.automated_error with reason sweep_exhausted. A creator's changes submission when nothing changed since the validator's own untouched rejection answers that rejection in the shape of an opened request (id, status, created_at, updated_at, collection_id, assignee).

review-verdict-acts-by-claim.text: POST /v1/collections/:id/validation-result with the review flow on: a verdict acts only from its request's current claim (claimId), on the collection that request names, in the transaction that settles the request; a rejection rejects the pending review or opens a rejected one, a pass reopens only the validator's own rejection, and neither touches a review a curator decided since the request started. Each such write is recorded in the operator audit as the validator. Upstream acts on the latest start's validationId.

newsletter-email-checked.text: POST /v1/newsletter: the node refuses a body without an email, an email that is no address (at most 254 characters, no space, control character, comma, semicolon or angle bracket, a local part of at most 64 characters and a domain of two or more labels), a source of more than 100 characters or with a control character, or a body that is not JSON, with 400 and a fixed message that repeats nothing of the body, and a body over 4 KiB with 413; it forwards nothing then. It forwards the email trimmed and lowercased and stores none. Upstream forwards whatever the body holds and answers {ok:true}.

newsletter-forward-failure.text: POST /v1/newsletter with the newsletter settings: the node waits for the newsletter service through a client that follows no redirect, so its key reaches no other host, and answers 502 {ok:false, data:{}, error:'The newsletter service did not take the subscription'} when the service answers other than 2xx, redirects or doesn't answer, with nothing of the service's answer. Upstream answers {ok:true} whatever the service answers. Without the settings both answer {ok:true}.

newsletter-budgets.text: POST /v1/newsletter takes, from one source address, at most 10 subscriptions an hour (checked before the body is read), of one email at most 3 a day and through the node at most 1,000 an hour; beyond, 429 {ok:false, data:{}, error:'Too many requests, try again in a minute'} with Retry-After, the seconds until one fits. Upstream bounds none.

cors-allow-list.text: Every builder route answers a cross-origin request from CORS_ORIGIN's list as upstream does: a listed origin is echoed in Access-Control-Allow-Origin, another origin gets none, answers vary by Origin and none allows credentials. The node writes the header names of Vary and Access-Control-Expose-Headers in lowercase; its preflight answers 200 (upstream 204) without Access-Control-Expose-Headers, allows the methods the routes answer (or CORS_METHOD's) and the headers they read (content-type, range, x-identity-timestamp, x-identity-metadata, x-identity-auth-chain-0 to -9, the validator's two signature headers, authorization) where upstream allows *, and lets a browser keep it for a day. Unset, CORS_ORIGIN is the Decentraland front-ends and http://localhost:<port> (upstream: every origin); a CORS_ORIGIN pattern the node can't compile, a list that names nothing or a CORS_METHOD method the routes don't answer stops the node at startup.

review-rate-limit-shape.text: The review routes' budgets per signed wallet, 30 writes (validations, appeal, comments) and 120 timeline reads a minute, spent before the review flow's flag is read, are token buckets refilled continuously (upstream: windows of one minute): a caller over one gets upstream's 429 body with Retry-After, the seconds until a request fits (upstream: until its window ends), and without upstream's RateLimit and RateLimit-Policy headers.

request-budgets.text: Every builder route spends, before anything else, from its source address's budget of 3,000 reads (GET, HEAD) or 2,400 writes a minute, and every signed route, once its signature verifies and before its body or the database, from its wallet's budget of 2,400 reads or 1,200 writes a minute; a listing of items spends one more read per 20 rows and per 64 KiB of item documents before it reads them, and is refused when its budgets can't pay that at once; a listing of curations or of an address's collections, or of a wallet's drafts (its newest 5,000), spends one more read per 20 rows once answered; and GET /v1/addresses and the public collection search 50 more; an item or collection save spends one more write token per 16 KiB of its body, and its KiB, at least 4, from its wallet's day of 1 GiB and its upload source's day of 2 GiB of saved documents; beyond a budget, 429 {ok:false, data:{}, error:'Too many requests, try again in a minute'} with Retry-After, the seconds until a request fits. A request from no address or an internal one (every request behind a gateway HTTP_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS doesn't list) spends no source budget. Upstream bounds only the review routes. A request body is bounded to what its route takes: 256 KiB for an item save, 2 MiB for a collection save, a terms acceptance and a publication, the upload routes their own, and 64 KiB elsewhere (413 unread).

wallet-storage-bound.text: POST /v1/items/:id/files and POST /v1/items/:id/videos refuse, before the body is read, an upload whose signer's uploads hold, apart from files a published item names, 100,000 files, or could hold past 5,000,000,000 bytes with it: the body's declared length, else the route's largest body, counts as stored, and a declared length past the route's body is refused at once with the route's own 413; 413 {ok:false, data:{maxBytes} or {maxFiles}, error:"The wallet's unpublished files reached their limit"}. Every wallet's together are bounded the same way by BUILDER_UNPUBLISHED_MAX_BYTES (1,000,000,000,000 unset) and BUILDER_UNPUBLISHED_MAX_FILES (10,000,000 unset); past either, 507 {ok:false, data:{maxBytes} or {maxFiles}, error:"The node's unpublished files reached their limit"}. The node counts the unpublished uploads in the background, one count at a time, and keeps each count a minute, so a publication frees them within a minute. An upload source (the client's address, an IPv6 address widened to its /48) may send 20 GiB and 100,000 files of uploads a day, and a wallet 50,000 files from any address, each checked before the body and charged with what the upload actually sent once it ends, whatever its outcome; once every wallet's unpublished uploads hold half the node's bound in bytes or files, each byte and file an upload source sends costs its day ten times. While a day is spent, 429 {ok:false, data:{}, error:'Too many requests, try again in a minute'} with Retry-After. Upstream bounds no wallet's, address's or node's storage.

curation-notice-inert-text.text: Creator text in the curators' Slack notices (a collection's name, a comment, an appeal note) carries a zero-width space around each formatting mark (*, _, ~, `) and after each :, . and @, so Slack shows it as written and turns none of it into a link, a mention, an emoji or formatting; upstream escapes only &, < and >.

Upstream takes any strings, up to 40,000 of them, and stores nothing.
